steps.action: Make the eleven scripts/*-check.sh scripts work where Docker is behind sudo and where cargo builds outside ./target. (1) Create scripts/common.sh, a bash file that a script sources. It starts with `#!/usr/bin/env bash` and a `# shellcheck shell=bash` line is not necessary when the shebang is present. It expects the caller to set `ROOT` first; give it a clear error when `ROOT` is not set (use `: "${ROOT:?scripts/common.sh: set ROOT before you source this file}"`). It does three things. (a) Docker command: `read -r -a DOCKER_CMD <<<"${DOCKER:-docker}"`; then check the first word with `command -v "${DOCKER_CMD[0]}" >/dev/null` and, when it is missing, print `missing required tool: <word>` to stderr and exit 1; then define `docker() { command "${DOCKER_CMD[@]}" "$@"; }`. The word `command` is necessary: without it the function calls itself without end when DOCKER is not set. A comment says: some machines put Docker behind sudo; run a script with DOCKER="sudo docker". (b) Target directory: `TARGET_DIR="$(cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 --manifest-path "$ROOT/Cargo.toml" | sed -n 's/.*"target_directory":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')"`; when `TARGET_DIR` is empty, print `cannot find the cargo target directory` to stderr and exit 1. A comment says: cargo can build outside ./target, through CARGO_TARGET_DIR or build.target-dir in a cargo config. (c) `S3ARMOR="$TARGET_DIR/debug/s3armor"`. If shellcheck reports SC2034 for a variable that only the caller uses, add `export` to that variable or one `# shellcheck disable=SC2034` line with a reason; do not add other disable lines. (2) In each of the eleven scripts, add these two lines directly after the existing `ROOT=` line and before any use of docker or of the binary: `# shellcheck source=scripts/common.sh` and `. "$ROOT/scripts/common.sh"`. (3) In each script, replace each `"$ROOT/target/debug/s3armor"` with `"$S3ARMOR"`. There are 23 such uses. One more place names `target/debug/s3armor` in a comment or message: change that text so it stays true (the binary comes from the cargo target directory). (4) Do not change any `docker` call site: the function takes them over. Do not change the `for tool in docker cargo ...` loops. Keep each script executable. Run the done check and read its output.
